title: Patient Financial Account Late Fee Terms
content:
On the Patient Financial Account the late fee is posted once per past-due statement when no payment is received by the late-fee day. The late-fee day falls a set number of calendar days after the statement date; the number of late fees on one account in any rolling 12 months is capped; and a partial payment of a set share of the statement balance before the late-fee day prevents the fee. A late fee amount of 0.00 means the fee is not charged on that class.

| Financial class (tier) | Late fee (USD) | Days after statement date before past due | Maximum late fees per rolling 12 months | Partial payment that prevents the fee (% of statement balance) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Medicaid Managed Care Account | 0.00 | 45 | 0 | 50.00 |
| Self-Pay Account | 15.00 | 45 | 4 | 50.00 |
| Medicare Part B Account | 0.00 | 45 | 0 | 50.00 |
| Medicare Advantage Account | 0.00 | 45 | 0 | 50.00 |
| Commercial HMO/EPO Account | 10.00 | 45 | 3 | 50.00 |
| Commercial PPO/POS Account | 10.00 | 45 | 3 | 50.00 |
| High-Deductible Health Plan Account | 10.00 | 45 | 3 | 50.00 |

Terms explained:

- The patient on a Medicaid Managed Care, Medicare Part B or Medicare Advantage account is charged no late fee: the fee is 0.00 and the yearly maximum is 0.
- The patient on a Self-Pay Account may be charged 15.00 per past-due statement, at most 4 times in a rolling 12 months; the patient on a commercial class (HMO/EPO, PPO/POS or High-Deductible Health Plan) may be charged 10.00, at most 3 times.
- Hypothetical example: on a statement balance of 240.00, a payment of 120.00 before the late-fee day is 50.00 percent of the balance and prevents the fee; a payment of 119.99 does not.
